claim: Tissue cells tessellate approximately as hexagons / as a froth, the configuration that partitions area with least perimeter.

primary_quotes.text: the general resemblance between a cellular tissue and a 'froth' ...

in dividing a closed space into a given number of chambers by means of partition-walls, the least possible area of these partition-walls, taken together, can only be attained when they meet together in groups of three, at equal angles, that is to say at angles of 120 degrees.

The hexagonal pattern is illustrated among organisms in countless cases, but those in which the pattern is perfectly regular, by reason of perfect uniformity of force and perfect equality of the individual cells, are not so numerous. The hexagonal epithelium-cells of the pigment layer of the eye, external to the retina, are a good example.

In an ordinary columnar epithelium, such as that of the intestine ... the cells are less uniform in size, small cells are apt to be intercalated among the larger, and the perfect symmetry is accordingly lost.

the rule still holds that only three partitions (in surface view) meet in a point; and at their point of meeting the walls are for a short distance manifestly curved, so as to permit the junction to take place at or nearly at the normal angle of 120 degrees.
where there is greater and more irregular variation in size, the cells will be on the average hexagonal, but some will have fewer and some more sides than six.
just as the closely packed hexagons gave the minimal extent of boundary in a plane, so the actual solid figure ... might be that which, for a given solid content, gives the minimum of surface.

C1_mean_six_froth.statement: A tissue is a trivalent planar froth: mean polygon side number is 6 (exactly 6 - 6*chi/F), with a spread of 5- and 7-gons.
C1_mean_six_froth.test: segmented specimen: three-way vertices fraction, mean n of interior cells, mu2 = var(n)
C1_mean_six_froth.pass_criterion: |<n> - 6| <= 0.15 for interior cells after border exclusion; >= 90 % of junctions trivalent

C2_hexagonal_optimum.statement: Among equal-area partitions the regular hexagonal honeycomb has least perimeter (Hales 2001); a tissue approaches it.
C2_hexagonal_optimum.test: excess perimeter eps = L_total / L_honeycomb(same cell areas) - 1, and per-cell shape index p = P/sqrt(A) vs regular-hexagon 3.7224
C2_hexagonal_optimum.pass_criterion: eps <= 0.10 (tissue within 10 % of the isoperimetric honeycomb bound for its own area distribution)

C3_near_regular_hexagons.statement: Cells are 'approximately hexagons' — read strictly, the modal class is hexagonal and most cells are 6-gons.
C3_near_regular_hexagons.test: hexagon fraction p6 of interior cells vs honeycomb (1.0), vs Gibson 2006 proliferating-epithelium Markov fixed point (0.464), vs normal adult corneal endothelium clinical norm (0.55-0.70)
C3_near_regular_hexagons.pass_criterion: p6 is the modal class AND p6 >= 0.5 for the strict reading; p6 in [0.4, 0.7] for the froth reading

equations.name: Euler trivalent-froth side-sum
equations.formula: 3V = 2E,  sum_i n_i = 2E,  V - E + F = chi  =>  sum_i n_i = 6F - 6 chi;  <n> = 6 - 6 chi / F
equations.variables: V vertices, E edges, F faces (cells), n_i sides of cell i, chi Euler characteristic (0 periodic, 2 sphere, 1 disc with boundary counted as a face)
equations.source: Thompson p. 325 'on the average hexagonal'; Weaire & Rivier 1984 Sec. 2

equations.name: Second moment of the polygon distribution
equations.formula: mu2 = sum_n p_n (n - 6)^2 = (1/F) sum_i n_i^2 - 36 (when <n> = 6);  mu2 = 0 iff every cell is a hexagon

equations.name: Isoperimetric honeycomb bound (least perimeter)
equations.formula: P_n(A) = 2 sqrt(n A tan(pi/n));  P_6(A) = 2 (12)^(1/4) sqrt(A) = 3.7224 sqrt(A);  P_6^4 = 192 A^2 < P_4^4 = 256 A^2 < P_3^4 = 432 A^2;  Hales: L_total >= (1/2) sum_i P_6(A_i) for any partition into cells of areas A_i (equal-area case)
equations.variables: P perimeter, A area, L_total total edge length (each edge shared by two cells)
equations.source: Thompson p. 330; Hales 2001 Discrete Comput. Geom. 25:1

equations.name: Lewis's law (size-topology)
equations.formula: <A_n> = A_6 (1 + lambda (n - 6)),  Lewis 1928: lambda = 1/4 i.e. <A_n> = A_6 (n - 2)/4

equations.name: Aboav-Weaire law (neighbour topology)
equations.formula: m(n) = (6 - a) + (6a + mu2)/n,  a ~ 1.2 for froths;  sum rule: sum_n n p_n m(n) = 36 + mu2
equations.variables: m(n) mean side number of the neighbours of an n-gon

equations.name: Division topology (Gibson 2006)
equations.formula: n-cell divides -> daughters s1 + s2 = n + 4 (each daughter: k + 3 and n - 2 - k + 3 sides), the two neighbours cut by the new wall gain one side each;  total sides +6 per +1 cell, so <n> = 6 is preserved; Markov fixed point p = (0.029, 0.289, 0.464, 0.208, 0.010) for n = 4..8
equations.variables: k undivided sides inherited by daughter 1

state_variables: cell polygon class n_i (number of neighbours = number of sides)

boundary_conditions.simulation: periodic (torus, chi = 0) Voronoi / Lloyd relaxation on an L x L box
boundary_conditions.specimen: finite micrograph window; cells touching the image border are excluded from polygon-class statistics (interior cells only); neighbour counts use the full segmentation

parameter_regime.meaning: positional disorder of the hexagonal seed lattice (fraction of lattice spacing)
parameter_regime.effect: p6 falls monotonically from 1 to the Poisson-Voronoi limit ~0.29; mu2 rises from 0 to ~1.78

parameter_regime.meaning: Lloyd / centroidal-Voronoi relaxation steps (froth relaxation toward least perimeter)
parameter_regime.effect: lowers excess perimeter and mu2, raises p6

parameter_regime.meaning: number of cells on the torus

counterclaim_2026.who: Gibson et al. 2006; Farhadifar et al. 2007
counterclaim_2026.text: Epithelial polygon distributions are froth-like but not simply 'hexagons tile best': proliferating epithelia have a characteristic polygon spectrum (substantial pentagon/heptagon fractions) explained by division topology, not by perimeter minimisation alone. Thompson's froth analogy survives, his implied hexagonal optimum does not describe growing tissue.
